title: CERN begins LHC shutdown for upgrades
seoTitle: CERN begins LHC shutdown for upgrades
subtitle: Update aims to boost intensity and magnetic field strength.
excerpt: CERN has started replacing key magnets in the Large Hadron Collider as part of its high‑luminosity upgrade.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
CERN has begun the process of powering down the Large Hadron Collider. The step is part of replacing some of the most critical magnets in the machine, integrating a high‑luminosity upgrade project.

With the installation of new superconducting magnets, the facility will generate fields about 40% stronger. This improvement will allow particle beams to be squeezed more tightly before they collide.

The expectation is to produce a much larger number of collisions for the ATLAS and CMS experiments. This will give physicists a significantly broader window to observe and study the fundamental workings of the universe.

With information from ScienceDaily.
